vectors.description: A non-exiting owned process receives SIGTERM, then SIGKILL; lifecycle work remains bounded, starts no replacement, and retains the live lease.
Closing twice is harmless and later ensure requests remain on direct compilation without starting a process.
A ready owned process with the same compatibility digest is reused without another reservation or start.
A connected compile error is preserved when a follow-up probe proves that the owned server remains responsive.
Concurrent ensure requests are serialized so one compatible owned process is started and then reused.
A failed compatibility digest remains on direct compilation instead of repeatedly attempting the same unavailable cache.
Shutdown removes only the exact lease bytes written by this instance and preserves a replacement owner.
A changed compatibility digest stops the old owned process before starting and leasing a replacement.
A lease created after startup probing prevents admission, preserves the foreign bytes, stops the owned process, and falls back.
A trusted lease whose owner or server process is alive is preserved and forces direct compilation without starting or adopting its process.
Malformed or noncanonical lease bytes are preserved and force direct compilation.
An escaping or link-traversing lease path fails before lifecycle work begins.
Failure to reserve isolated loopback capacity starts no process and selects direct compilation.
A process that never becomes probe-ready is stopped within the startup bound and direct compilation is selected.
A trusted exact lease with a provably dead owner is removed before a new owned server is started.
A process that exits before readiness is not leased and selects direct compilation.
Unexpected exit clears only the owned lease and a later ensure starts a replacement for the same digest.
A connected compile failure followed by a failed probe stops the owned process and retries through direct compilation.
